2.1     Software Quality Models and Frameworks                           tions. The company specializes in delivering customized software

work prescribes how to measure specific attributes, and bench-           nerstone of their quality assurance strategy. Their continuous in-
marks provide industry standards or historical data for comparison       tegration pipeline implements a systematic validation sequence
[ISO/IEC 2011, Wagner et al. 2012].                                      that includes: compilation and build verification, unit testing of

4.1     Code Quality Metrics                                                           feedback about test thoroughness. High coverage values, while not
Code quality metrics focus on aspects that can be analyzed without                     guaranteeing test effectiveness, indicate that the LLM is capable of
test execution. At the most basic level, test compilation success                      generating tests that explore different code paths and conditions.
serves as a gateway - without it, no further evaluation is possible.                   However, these metrics must be considered alongside black box
Beyond compilation, these metrics assess maintainability through                       metrics that assess test design quality.
static analysis and proper test structure.
   Table 1 details the three code quality metrics. First, Test Compila-
tion Issues track the accuracy in handling external dependencies and
basic syntactic correctness, identifying critical issues that would
prevent tests from being integrated into existing codebases. These
issues establish the minimum requirements for generated tests to                       3 https://github.com/jacoco/jacoco

key testing techniques. Equivalence partitioning evaluates whether              for ensuring that automatically generated tests meet the quality

       Organizations need to maintain ongoing evaluation pro-                              Construct Validity: Our measurement framework relies on spe-
       cesses rather than relying on point-in-time assessments.                        cific metrics to evaluate test quality and LLM effectiveness. There is
     • Model Selection and Costs: While newer models like Claude                       a risk that these metrics may not fully capture all relevant aspects
       3.5 Sonnet and o1-Preview show impressive performance,                          of test quality or may not accurately reflect the actual value of LLM-
       they come with higher computational costs and latency. Ad-                      generated tests in industrial practice. We mitigate this threat in
       ditionally, tools like GitHub Copilot require per-seat licens-                  several ways: (1) combining both automated metrics and expert as-
       ing, which can be significant for larger teams. Organizations                   sessment to provide a more complete evaluation, (2) validating our
       must balance these costs against potential productivity gains.                  measurement framework with experienced QA professionals be-
     • Technical Investment: Success with these tools requires invest-                 fore deployment, and (3) incorporating feedback from practitioners
       ment in two key areas. First, as shown by our results, proper                   throughout the study period to refine our metrics.
       prompt engineering significantly impacts performance. Sec-                          Internal Validity: The observed improvements in LLM perfor-
       ond, developers need training to effectively use them, partic-                  mance over time could be influenced by factors other than actual
       ularly in understanding prompt engineering principles and                       evolution in LLM capabilities. In particular, our iterative refinement
       best practices.                                                                 of prompting strategies might confound the results. To address this,
     • Data Privacy Risks: When testing involves client code or pro-                   we: (1) maintain consistent base prompts across evaluation periods,
       prietary information, organizations must evaluate how LLMs                      (2) clearly document any prompt modifications, and (3) validate
       handle this data. Solutions might include air-gapped environ-                   significant changes in performance through multiple test runs.
       ments or local LLM deployments for sensitive code, though                           External Validity: While our study provides insights from a real-
       these come with their own technical and cost implications.                      world industrial setting, it is primarily based on experiences from
     • Expert Oversight: Despite the high scores achieved in our                       a single organization and specific types of software projects. The
       metrics, expert review remains essential. The black box met-                    effectiveness of our framework and findings may not generalize to
       rics in particular show that while LLMs have improved in                        organizations with different development practices, project types,
       applying testing techniques, they don’t yet match human                         or quality requirements. To strengthen external validity, we: (1)
       expertise in test design decisions.                                             designed the framework to be adaptable to different organizational
                                                                                       contexts, and (2) focused on industry-standard tools and practices
   These findings suggest that while LLM-based test generation                         that are common across organizations.
tools are becoming increasingly viable for industrial use, their suc-                      Reliability: The expert assessment component of our framework
cessful adoption requires both systematic evaluation frameworks                        inherently involves subjective judgment, which could affect the re-
and realistic expectations. Companies should view these tools as                       producibility of our results. We implement two measures to enhance
aids to augment developer productivity rather than complete re-                        reliability: (1) establishing clear, documented evaluation criteria
placements for human testing expertise.                                                for expert reviewers, (2) maintaining detailed documentation of
                                                                                       all measurement procedures, tools, and decision criteria to enable
                                                                                       replication.
8    THREATS TO VALIDITY
                                                                                           While these threats cannot be completely eliminated, we be-
As with any empirical study, particularly one involving emerging                       lieve our mitigation strategies provide reasonable confidence in our
technologies like LLMs, there are several potential threats to the                     findings.
validity of our findings.
